messages:
Maya: heads-up: the python sampleapp generator is emitting 'Any' for nested object schemas which breaks strict mypy/pyright checks in our onboarding examples

Maya: tiny repro in sampleapp: 
```python
# generated by pydantic_v1 target
class GeneratedResponse(BaseModel):
    id: str
    metadata: Any  # should be TypedDict or nested model when schema has properties

# user code in stream handler
async for ev in client.stream_responses(...):
    meta = ev.model_output.metadata
    # mypy complains: "Expression of type "Any" should be avoided" and downstream calls show no attribute errors
    name = meta.get('name')  # no autocomplete, no static checks
```

Liam: can confirm. ran mypy on sampleapp after fresh codegen and lots of helper dict accesses lose type info. locally I just did typing.cast(Dict[str, Any], meta) to proceed but that defeats the point

Zach: is the generator treating 'type: object' without explicit properties differently? I think the fallback to Any happens when the schema uses additionalProperties or has free-form. If properties are present we should emit a nested model or TypedDict by default

Maya: in our OpenAPI-ish specs we often have schemas like:
```json
{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"labels":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}}}
```
which should ideally become: GeneratedResponse.metadata: TypedDict('Metadata', {'name': str, 'labels': Dict[str, str]}) or a Pydantic model

Ana: feature request: add a codegen flag `--prefer-typed-dict` and `--emit-nested-models` so sampleapps can opt into stricter typing. also important: async stub signatures should use AsyncIterator[GeneratedResponse] instead of AsyncIterator[Any] for stream endpoints

deploy-bot: CI: sampleapp/mypy-check  FAILED  2 errors (mypy) :eyes:

Zach: I'll prototype changes: 1) when schema.type == 'object' and properties present -> emit TypedDict; 2) if additionalProperties exists -> map to Dict[str, T]; 3) update stub generator to use concrete response types for streaming endpoints. Opening WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/802

Liam: nice. can you add a small regression test that binds generated types into a tiny sampleapp stream handler and runs mypy in CI? That way the onboarding quickstart won't regress again

Maya: agreed. onboarding experience hit me bad when I first ran the sample app. also worth a docs blurb in the Python SDK "Typing and codegen" section explaining the flags and recommended patterns for nested freeform maps vs strict models

Ana: I'll update the devex checklist to include a mypy job for sampleapp and a note to mention the new flags in quickstart. assigning INF-1299 to track follow-up

Zach: PR updated with typed dict emitter + stub fix. still sorting some edge cases where schema uses anyOf/oneOf -> fallback strategy needed. tagging @Liam for review on the mypy CI job

Maya: thanks all. once merged I'll re-run my sampleapp branch and paste results here. if anyone runs into mypy noise after merge ping the thread and we'll triage

Liam: adding CI job now (mypy + pyright sanity). PR/CI job linked in ticket INF-1299

Maya: happy path confirmed locally after pulling Zach's branch: typed fields show up, mypy no longer complains, and autocompletion works in VSCode :tada:

Ana: dropping a short note in #devex when the PR lands so onboarding docs can be updated

Zach: thanks team. follow-ups: documentation blurb, CI job, resolve anyOf/oneOf mapping rules, and consider an opt-in strict mode in codegen config

Maya: perfect. I'll close my onboarding feedback now. cheers! :thumbsup:
